recipes.name: Mississippi Mud Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (12 ounce) container frozen whipped topping, thawed
1 (3.9 ounce) package instant chocolate pudding mix
1 (3.4 ounce) package instant butterscotch pudding mix

steps.text: Thoroughly blend graham cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup sugar, and butter. Press firmly in bottom of 9x13-inch pan.
Blend half the whipped topping, 3/4 cup sugar, and softened cream cheese together in a bowl; spread mixture on top of prepared crust.
Whip chocolate pudding, butterscotch pudding, and milk together; spread on top of cream cheese mixture. Top with remaining whipped topping.

raw_recipe.headline: Mississippi Mud Pie
raw_recipe.description: A homemade graham cracker crust is slathered with a sweetened whipped topping and cream cheese mixture, layered with gooey chocolate and butterscotch pudding.

review.reviewBody:
We made it just like the recipe says, and it was delicious, even though my little brother complained saying the butterscotch pudding tasted coffee-like.
MAKE SURE YOU LET THE PUDDING SIT. I have made pudding before, and in a hurry I had not let it sit at all, I kept mixing continuously. Letting my pudding sit for two minutes while my mom lectured me on how to layer the pie right was the best food technique I've ever learned! It will actually thicken into pudding, instead of how liquidy it looks when you add the two cups of milk. I was also surprised when the crust tasted like brown sugar, though it didn't stick well to the cream-cheese mixture.

One of my go to favorites! Before making it I highly suggest you read the reviews. I've made it multiple times and here is what I do. I've never made a full 9X13 dish of it so I can't judge on how that would turn out. Instead, I buy 2 Oreo or chocolate pie crust in the baking isle. (This saves time on making the crust.) PLUS, the bonus is this makes 2 pies! Yes, use the 3 cups of milk. I use 2 packages of chocolate pudding since I'm not a fan of butterscotch. The must do thing to make this a success is to mix the milk and pudding mix together and let it SIT AT 5-6 MINUTES to thicken BEFORE assembling. After adding the final layer of Cool Whip wrap securely and freeze. Sit it in the fridge a few hours before serving. It may not cut completely cleanly (depending on how long it has been out of the freezer) but it is good! Just keep it cold. I've made this before Thanksgiving and had 1 Thanksgiving and saved the 2nd pie for Christmas. Great for a pot-luck. Super easy, super inexpensive and always a hit!

When I was little, my aunt Jen would come to visit around thanksgiving and Christmas time, and would always bring a Mississippi mud pie. Fast forward and I’m now a 27 y/o bachelor living on my own and for years have never been able to replicate her recipe. Well after a few alterations, this is it, just as I remember it. I stuck true to the recipe, except for the butterscotch pudding which I ended up omitting, and I also added in crushed pecans on the cool whip and cream cheese layer, and on the top layer. I used a Pyrex dish to make this in, and after pouring in the graham cracker crumb mixture and pressing it in (I used a spoon to do so), I stuck it in the oven @ 350 for 20 or so minutes. This helped the crust solidify into a solid piece and added an extra crispness to the overall recipe.

I changed the crust to 1 cup AP flour, 1/2 cup butter cut into tablespoon pieces, 1 cup chopped walnuts and 1/2 cup sugar. Mix well until crumbly. Press into 9×12 greased baking pan and bake for 17 minutes at 350⁰. Let cool before adding other layers.

Scrumptious!
I made a few changes that made it more yummy: Multiplied the cream cheese layer by 1.5. Did the same with the pudding layer. Sprinkled peanut dust and 2 crushed SKOR candy bars on top of the cool whip layer. This thing disappeared fast! My husband insisted that I sneak a piece to save for him for the next day before everyone devoured it.

Good recipe! Super easy! I changed a few things, I made my own Oreo crust (crushed up a whole thing of Oreos, minus the middle, and mixed with 12 tbs of melted butter and baked for about 10 mins at 350) and instead of using butterscotch I used vanilla. I used 2 9in pie tins to make it in and was a perfect amount. I will make this again the same way I made it the first time, but instead of using the frozen whipped topping, I will use canned whipped cream because the frozen stuff melts and just doesn't look pretty even though it tastes good.

This is a good but very rich and sweet dessert. I used gluten free graham crackers and discovered that one box only made 1 cup of crumbs so I halved the crust ingredients and put them in a 9x9 square pan. I intended to fill as needed but used the entire filling amount for the square pan. If I were to make this again for a 13x9 I would double the cream cheese layer. I also added extra whipped topping to the top layer. I had bought the big container of whipped topping so there may have been a slight difference in my conversion of ounces to cups.

So good! Family loved it as it was nice and light after a turkey dinner and not too sweet. The only thing I did different was eliminate the milk as I cooked pudding as per package directions the night before. Highly recommend as it prevents it from becoming runny. I also layered chocolate and butterscotch pudding instead of combining.
You can make this pie even easier, buy the graham crust pie. I get Keebler pie crust and quick. It’s very tasty and you don’t need the oven for the crust.

I added to the recipe by adding about 1/4 cup walnuts chopped very fine to the graham cracker crust mixture and once the crust was formed I stuck it in the oven for 5 minutes. After everything was done I sprinkled just a few chopped walnuts on the top and it turned out really good.

I absolutely love this dessert - it’s often requested by my family. Instead of a mix of chocolate pudding and butterscotch pudding, I use two boxes of butterscotch. It’s delicious this way! I’ve also made it with two boxes of chocolate pudding too, cans that’s also fantastic.
Made it for a summer party. Couldn't get butterscotch pudding so I substituted banana. Huge hit! Can't wait to make it again. Thanks for sharing.
Should have put nuts in it
Loved This Recipe! I Added Finely Chopped Pecans To The Crust.
We couldn't wait to eat this dish from my grandmother at family functions. I carry this on in her memory!! A must have!!
Simple to make…. All 10s from the judges!!!
My son has asked for this to be his “birthday cake” for the last ten years! My whole family loves it and gets excited when I make it!
wonderful and great for company dessert also, could eat it for any time so good, easy to make
